title: Solving Basic Trig Equations
short: Find every solution in one period, then all solutions.
trouble: Students stop at the calculator's one answer and miss the second solution in [0, 2π).

blocks.html: An identity is true for every angle; an equation like $2\sin x - 1 = 0$ is true only for some. Solving one uses everything from reference angles and inverse trig functions. The new part is finding all the solutions.

Isolate the trig function. Find the reference angle from the size of the value. List every angle in one period, $[0, 2\pi)$, in the quadrants where the sign is right. For all solutions, add whole periods: $+2k\pi$ for sine and cosine, $+k\pi$ for tangent.

On the unit circle, $\sin x = \frac{1}{2}$ means the point is at height $\frac{1}{2}$. The horizontal line $y = \frac{1}{2}$ crosses the circle at two points, one in Quadrant I and its mirror image in Quadrant II. A calculator's $\sin^{-1}$ can only report one of them, the one in its range. Then every full turn repeats both.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.cap: The line $y = \frac{1}{2}$ crosses the sine wave twice in every period of $2\pi$.

blocks.title: Two solutions
blocks.q: Solve $2\sin x - 1 = 0$ on $[0, 2\pi)$, then give all solutions.
steps: Reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$. Sine is positive in Quadrants I and II: $x = \frac{\pi}{6}$ and $x = \pi - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{6}$.
All solutions: $x = \frac{\pi}{6} + 2k\pi$ or $x = \frac{5\pi}{6} + 2k\pi$, for any integer $k$.

blocks.title: A negative value
steps: Cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III: $\pi - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{6}$ and $\pi + \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{7\pi}{6}$.

blocks.title: Tangent
steps: Reference angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$; tangent is negative in Quadrants II and IV.
$x = \frac{3\pi}{4}$ and $x = \frac{7\pi}{4}$, exactly $\pi$ apart, as tangent's period predicts.

blocks.html: Stopping at the one answer a calculator gives. $\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\pi}{6}$ is only one solution. Draw the horizontal (for sine) or vertical (for cosine) line on the unit circle and count where it crosses: usually twice per turn. Check each answer by substituting it back.

blocks.name: unitcircle

opts.task: Find the other angle in $[0^\circ, 360^\circ)$ whose sine is $\frac{1}{2}$.

blocks.cap: Same height, other side of the circle.
